reason: Payment intent references, update times, an order reference key and attempt method, status and amount summaries identify no person or company.
sql: SELECT pi.id, pi."updatedAt", pi.metadata ->> 'orderRef' AS order_ref, array_agg(pa.payment_method_kind || ':' || pa.status || ':' || pa.captured_amount_cents::text ORDER BY pa.payment_method_kind) AS attempts FROM payment_orchestrator.payment_intent pi JOIN payment_orchestrator.payment_attempt pa ON pa.payment_intent_id = pi.id WHERE pi.status = 'AUTHORIZED' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM payment_orchestrator.payment_attempt c WHERE c.payment_intent_id = pi.id AND c.status = 'CAPTURED') GROUP BY pi.id, pi."updatedAt", pi.metadata ORDER BY pi."updatedAt"

reason: A count per operational status over the whole relation selects no person or company.
sql: SELECT status, count(*) AS n FROM payment_orchestrator.payment_intent GROUP BY status ORDER BY status

reason: A CTE over product codes and quantities returns ordinary inventory data.
sql: WITH low AS (SELECT sku, quantity FROM inventory.stock WHERE quantity < 10) SELECT sku, quantity FROM low ORDER BY quantity

reason: Ranking products by price inside a category discloses ordinary catalog data.
sql: SELECT sku, category, price, rank() OVER (PARTITION BY category ORDER BY price DESC) AS price_rank FROM inventory.catalog

reason: A CASE bucket over quantities with a concatenated label stays within product data.
sql: SELECT sku || '-' || size_code AS variant, CASE WHEN quantity > 100 THEN 'high' ELSE 'low' END AS level, coalesce(reserved, 0) AS reserved FROM inventory.stock

reason: Daily order counts and totals over the whole relation identify no customer.
sql: SELECT date_trunc('day', created_at) AS day, count(*) AS orders, sum(total_cents) AS total FROM sales.orders WHERE created_at >= now() - interval '7 days' GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1

reason: A derived table of per-status totals then averaged returns aggregates only.
sql: SELECT avg(t.total) AS average_total FROM (SELECT status, sum(total_cents) AS total FROM sales.orders GROUP BY status) t

reason: Aggregated free text written by or about customers can contain personal information.
sql: SELECT ticket_ref, string_agg(note_text, ' | ' ORDER BY noted_at) AS notes FROM support.ticket_notes GROUP BY ticket_ref

reason: A filtered count comparing a holder label with a supplied value tests an identifiable person's membership.

reason: A CTE alias cannot hide an email source.

reason: Aggregating email addresses still reads them.

reason: A whole JSON document stays opaque when wrapped in a cast or function.

reason: Advancing a sequence changes database state.

reason: A running total of refund amounts per day identifies no person or company.
